source.authors: Anderson CM, Wisenden BD, Craig CA, Stockwell CA
source.title: Consistent Antipredator Behavioral Responses among Populations of Red River Pupfish with Disparate Predator Communities

value: alarm cue significantly reduced post-stimulus water column position (Cue F1,140 = 21.170, p < 0.001); the direct and interactive effects of Population were not significant
units: categorical (ANCOVA effect of cue on position in water column)
method: single female fish in 37 L aquaria at 24 C (filled with dechlorinated tap water at 10 ppt salinity); stimulus delivered by a tube at the air stone, either conspecific skin alarm cue (epidermis blended in deionized water and diluted to 1 cm2 skin per 10 mL, stored in individual 10-mL doses) or water as the control; the volume delivered per trial and the control water's source are not printed; water column position recorded every 10 s for 5 min before and 5 min after the stimulus; ANCOVA with Cue and Population as factors and pre-stimulus behaviour as covariate
conditions: wild-sourced: females collected from five Red River sites (Table 1 n = 33, 22, 38, 38, 29; 160 fish; site 5 high predation risk with largemouth bass) and shipped to NDSU, held in 1135 L population-specific outdoor tanks at 10 ppt, at least 20 h acclimation before trials, 16 h:8 h light:dark, trials June to August 2020; 24 blocks of 10 aquaria, within each block two females from each of the five populations randomly assigned to the two treatments; analysis dropped one hyperactive fish and eight trials with no pre-stimulus movement, and per-treatment n after exclusions is not given; number and population of skin donors not stated; observer blinding not stated; same-section activity result: a Cue x Pre-stimulus activity interaction (F1,140 = 9.90; p = 0.002); Cue x Pre-stimulus behaviour interaction not significant for water column position; Population direct and interactive effects not significant for either variable
quote: Alarm cue caused a significant reduction in the post-stimulus water column position (Cue F1,140 = 21.170, p < 0.001; Table 2B), but the direct and interactive effects of Population were not significant (Table 2B, Figure 2B).
note: Classification: behavioural_response, a water-column position (freezing/refuge-type) change after a chemical cue with a water control; no other modality in the design.
